title: Mobile Website
h1: Mobile websites that keep customers with you on every phone
p1: As smartphone use keeps changing, WebAstral Infosystems extends your communication to mobile sites. Whether you are an SME or a large account, customers stay informed about your company and use your services from a phone — without zooming, waiting, or losing your brand.
h2: Dedicated mobile or responsive design, built around how people actually browse
p2: With our solutions you can support marketing campaigns, micro-payments, geo-location, tracking, QR codes, and social networks. We offer two paths: a dedicated mobile site, or a responsive design that keeps your identity while the layout adjusts to computer, tablet, and smartphone.
h3: What are the benefits of a mobile website?
points: One site, one customer experience on every device
A layout that fits any screen resolution
One URL that strengthens your SEO
Faster mobile browsing with a lighter design

workProcess.title: Research
workProcess.description: We study how your audience uses phones, what they need on the go, and where the current site slows them down.

workProcess.title: Strategy
workProcess.description: We choose dedicated mobile or responsive design so the experience matches your brand, campaigns, and SEO goals.

workProcess.title: Design
workProcess.description: We keep your visual identity and make type, tap targets, and navigation readable without pinch-zoom.

workProcess.title: Develop
workProcess.description: We lighten graphics and structure pages so they load quickly on slower mobile connections.

workProcess.title: Launch
workProcess.description: We test on real phones and tablets, then hand over a site your customers can use anywhere.

faqs.title: Should we build a dedicated mobile site or a responsive website?
faqs.description: Both work. A dedicated mobile site is built only for phones. Responsive design keeps one site and one brand, then adjusts the layout to computer, tablet, and smartphone. We recommend the option that fits your campaigns, content, and budget after a short discovery.

faqs.title: Will the mobile version still look like our brand?
faqs.description: Yes. Responsive design keeps the identity and design of your site while it adapts graphically for readability. The same brand shows on every device, with a lighter layout that is easier to use on a phone.

faqs.title: How do you make pages fast on slower mobile connections?
faqs.description: On the go, connections are often slower than a desktop. We display fewer heavy graphic elements, optimize images, and keep the layout light so people can read and move through the site without waiting.

faqs.title: Is one URL better for SEO?
faqs.description: Yes. A single URL and centralized content make it easier to rank and keep the customer journey consistent, whether someone arrives from search on a phone or a computer.

faqs.title: Can you rebuild our existing website for mobile?
faqs.description: We can build a mobile website from scratch or redo an old one. Timeline depends on how much of the current design, content, and features need to change. Share the live URL and we will give you a clear plan.

title: Parallax Web Design
h1: Parallax websites that pull visitors deeper as they scroll
p1: Parallax scrolling is bringing user experience to a new level of interactive visualization. We separate background and foreground so they move at different speeds, giving a sense of depth as people sail from bottom to top. Used well, it makes sites fluid, fun, and hard to leave.
h2: A graphical experience that tells a story while they scroll
p2: Our designers and developers explore new ways to make web design more attractive through motion and visual features. Parallax lets you surprise viewers with depth, guide them with a story, keep them on the page, spark curiosity, and give the site credibility through interactive visualization.
points: Surprise viewers with depth and animation
Guide visitors through a story on the page
Keep people scrolling through the full site

workProcess.title: Research
workProcess.description: We map the story you need to tell and where depth, motion, and pauses will help visitors stay with you.

workProcess.title: Story
workProcess.description: We structure sections so each scroll beat reveals the next layer of the brand narrative.

workProcess.title: Design
workProcess.description: We separate background and foreground graphics so the layout stays clear while layers move at different speeds.

workProcess.title: Motion
workProcess.description: We build fluid parallax, 2D and 3D animation, and scroll effects that feel smooth rather than distracting.

workProcess.title: Launch
workProcess.description: We test scrolling on real devices, then ship a site that impresses visitors with a unique navigation experience.

faqs.title: What is parallax web design?
faqs.description: Parallax separates visual elements of the background so they scroll at different speeds. That creates a sense of depth as visitors move from bottom to top, turning a normal page into an interactive visualization.

faqs.title: Will parallax still work for SEO?
faqs.description: Yes, when it is built as one coherent page with clear content. Curious visitors stay longer and scroll the full story, which helps engagement. We keep the structure readable for search engines while the motion does the visual work.

faqs.title: Is parallax only for e-commerce?
faqs.description: It works especially well when you need to hook customers with a story, including e-commerce, but any brand that wants a unique, fluid visit can use it. We match the intensity of motion to your product and audience.

faqs.title: Can you add parallax to an existing website?
faqs.description: Often yes. We review the current layout, then add layered sections and scroll effects where they help the story. If the site is too rigid, we rebuild the key pages so motion stays smooth.

faqs.title: How do you keep parallax from feeling slow?
faqs.description: We use light layers, controlled animation, and performance checks so scrolling stays fluid. The goal is a fun visit, not a heavy page that lags on phones.

title: Responsive Web Design
h1: Responsive websites that fit every screen without zooming
p1: Users are increasingly mobile and screens keep multiplying. Responsive web design remains the simple, flexible way to fit current and coming devices. The layout adjusts to the browser, tablet, smartphone, or connected TV so people get a full visit — without zoom, without a separate mobile site.
h2: One site, complete immersion on every terminal
p2: Beyond adapting to a phone, responsive design is a user experience: complete immersion regardless of the device. We usually map 3 to 4 templates to resolution families and use CSS so mobile users get a tailored layout, resized images, and reorganized content — with no redirects and low maintenance.
points: Simple, ergonomic navigation on every device
Content that is comfortable to read without zoom
Images that resize with the screen
No redirects, no OS detection, low maintenance

workProcess.title: Research
workProcess.description: We identify how your audience actually browses — phone, tablet, desktop, and what they need to do on each.

workProcess.title: Breakpoints
workProcess.description: We map 3 to 4 templates to resolution families so the layout reflows cleanly instead of shrinking in place.

workProcess.title: Design
workProcess.description: We plan type, tap targets, and navigation so the same brand stays readable from a wide monitor to a small phone.

workProcess.title: Develop
workProcess.description: We build fluid grids, flexible images, and CSS that serve the right layout without extra versions or redirects.

workProcess.title: Testing
workProcess.description: We check real devices and browsers so the experience stays fast, accessible, and easy to use everywhere.

faqs.title: What is responsive web design?
faqs.description: It is a site designed to adapt to different screen sizes and terminals — browser, tablet, smartphone, connected TV. The same URL and content reflow with CSS so people never need a separate mobile site or the zoom feature.

faqs.title: How many layouts do you design?
faqs.description: We usually design 3 to 4 templates mapped to families of resolutions. That keeps maintenance low while covering the devices your customers actually use.

faqs.title: Will visitors still need to zoom on a phone?
faqs.description: No. Type, images, and navigation are sized for the device. Mobile users get a tailored experience without pinch-zoom or a scaled-down desktop page.

faqs.title: Do you create a separate mobile website?
faqs.description: Responsive design avoids extra versions, redirects, and operating-system detection. One site, one set of content, lower maintenance — and a consistent brand on every screen.

faqs.title: Can you make our existing site responsive?
faqs.description: Yes. Timeline depends on how the current layout is built. We review the live site, then rework grids, images, and navigation so it reflows cleanly. Share the URL and we will outline the work.

title: User Experience Design
h1: UX that helps people reach their goal without friction
p1: Only successful experiences keep mature, demanding users engaged. UX design focuses on the whole visit — content, layout, and site architecture — so someone can buy, research, or complete a task without getting lost. We use collaborative, iterative methods so the product feels designed for the people who will actually use it.
h2: The right questions, then wireframes and prototypes
p2: We start by asking what your audience expects — for example, what should a travel site offer first, and how do those visitors actually behave? Then we place information areas on a wireframe to meet business goals, and build prototypes so practices are defined before the full visual design. That sequence keeps people on the site and leaves a better impression.
points: Collaborative, iterative design and collective intelligence
Content, architecture, and layout that help users finish their task
The right questions about audience behaviour before pixels are drawn
Wireframes that place information to meet business goals
Prototypes that define practices before the full build

faqs.title: How does collaboration work on a UX project?
faqs.description: We stay in direct contact throughout the process and work in short iterative cycles so changes land quickly. A researcher and a group of designers stay dedicated to the project so the product stays user-centered and on schedule.

faqs.title: What is a wireframe in a web project?
faqs.description: A wireframe is not a finished graphic of the site. It is an ergo-layout that places information areas on the page so business goals and audience expectations sit in the right order before visual design begins.

faqs.title: Why is research important in UX design?
faqs.description: Research shows the choices, requirements, and preferences of the people you want to reach. Those insights keep the product user-centered and help the team understand the business well enough to target the right customers.

faqs.title: Why do you prototype before the visual design?
faqs.description: Prototypes let you review flows, content placement, and practices on the site or application while they are still cheap to change. That step is how we define what to adopt before the full build.

faqs.title: Does UX work stop at launch?
faqs.description: No. Many factors matter during design and afterward. User feedback after launch is part of keeping people on the site, leaving a good impression, and refining the experience against web standards.

faqs.title: What is PPC?
faqs.description: PPC stands for Pay Per Click. It is a digital marketing strategy to buy traffic for your website. In this scenario, the advertiser pays a small fee each time one of your ads is clicked by the user. Search engine advertising is the most popular form of PPC. Even many social media platforms like Facebook also offer PPC models. You can promote your company in search results, on websites, and across social media platforms. PPC ads can also consist of text, videos, and pictures.

faqs.title: Will my target market click on my online PPC Ads?
faqs.description: Ads that appear on search results are published to target specific audiences and earn almost half of all page clicks. Users who click on paid ads are usually ready to make decisions and therefore more likely to buy products and services by comparison to an organic visitor. With PPC ads, you can target online users who are searching for any specific product or service. It can boost your sales and promote your business to a great extent.

faqs.title: How do I Budget my PPC Ads?
faqs.description: Your PPC services cost is calculated based on your bid, your targeting, and your ad quality. The amount of money you're willing to spend for a user to click on your ad is called your bid. You enter your bid into an ad auction and the highest bidder wins, so you could end up paying less than your bid amount, but never more. Targeting factors include all aspects of your goal, from the keywords you’re ranking for to the demographics of your audience.
